verified.root_cause:
When a task's PR is seen merged on GitHub, the code updates the merge record but never touches that task's open merge cards. Nothing in any merge path closes them. Three things follow:
(1) DependentBranches.mergedOnHost moves the merge record to 'merged' (last_outcome merged_on_host), logs 'pull request merged on the host' and calls ReviewedPrMerge.merged. It never looks at the task's open 'merge:left_open' cards: the head-moved card ('I merged it / Leave it open'), the rebuilt-without card ('Merge / Redo') and the conflict-notice card.
(2) None of the onMerged listeners in compose withdraws a card either. They log and emit, rebuild dependents, refresh the copy and drop the preview. The helpers that withdraw a merge card (openMergeCard plus humanRequest.withdraw in closeStaleNotice, closeConflictCard and closeRebuildConflictCard) run only from the conflict sweep. There is no generic 'task moved on' closer, so the card stays open through restarts. This breaks design section 3.8: 'A card whose task has moved on is closed with a line saying so'.
(3) The rebuild card's Merge on a PR that is already merged goes through applyRebuildMerge. approveInOrder skips a record that is already merged (merge.ts:1166), so it returns no records and mergeApproved never runs. The function then returns 'merging' with no merge_result, and mergeLeftOpenOutcome words it 'Merging #42.' (request-words.ts:1044). The UI shows that as 'Done: Merging #42.' for a PR that was merged at 06:29:51.
The chat's 'never merged' line comes from the stale card, not from the model on its own. The 06:16:25 chat call's open_requests fact quoted the open card in full: 'The critic accepted ..., but pull request #33 was not merged. #33 changed after the review...', marked [not yet mentioned]. The same facts listed the task as Merged and #33 under 'Already merged or closed'. The model repeated the app's own card, so withdrawing the card removes the cause.

verified.root_cause:
The press route does not look at the pull request's head before it answers. `ProjectPullRequests.merge()` takes the row from `view()`. In `view()`, `mergeOfRecord()` builds each row from the merge record alone and never compares the listed `pr.head.sha` with `record.reviewed_head_sha`. So a record waiting for the click reads `left_to_you`/`ready` with `canMerge: true`. The route then puts the person's approval on the records (`approveInOrder`) and starts `mergeApproved` in the background. It answers at once with `Merging ${names}.` (pull-requests.ts:656). The head move is found only later, inside the merge step: GitHub refuses the sha-pinned merge ("Head branch was modified", merge.ts:628 maps that to `head_moved`), or the folder check finds it. That step settles the record as `head_moved` with `headMovedWords`, files the card and sets the Tasks label. The Overview polls every 1.5 s and only then switches to "#40 is not merged yet: the row below says why."

The route already holds the moved head at the press: `view()` just called `listPullRequests`, which returns `head.sha`. It throws that away. W15-05 fixed the same kind of broken promise for the folder wait ("before, the press answered 'Merging #23.' while nothing could merge"). The head move was left out. W15B-40's "as designed" covers only the poll not showing the move before a press. It does not cover the press answer. Design §5 rules 4 ("True now") and 9 ("No promises the code does not keep") are broken.

Reproduced off the bench with the unit-test world (MemoryGitHost, real store), script /tmp/frbench/l3g3/repro.mts. The reviewed head was sha-fr/packing and the listed head sha-new-commit-on-github. The row showed `{state:"left_to_you",canMerge:true}` and the press answered `{"state":"queued","sentence":"Merging #1.","order":[1]}`. The result was the same at 7d6b34a and at 112227c. The live evidence agrees: the answer came in 998 ms with "Merging #40.", screenshot 74 shows "Merging #40.", and screenshot 75 shows the refusal sentence on the row with "#40 is not merged yet". The Merge button stayed visible until the step settled.

In ProjectPullRequests.merge(), for task rows: keep the listed head of each PR from the `listPullRequests` read in `view()` (an internal map from number to head.sha), or re-read it with `host.getPullRequest`. For each record in the chain with a non-empty `reviewed_head_sha` that differs from the listed head, do not answer "Merging #N." blind.

The route cannot refuse on the sha difference alone. The merge step follows a head that keeps exactly the reviewed change (GitHub's Update branch, main merged in: `keepsOwnChange`, merge.ts:1417-1435).

Preferred: run the step's verdict in the foreground for that press. Await `merge.mergeApproved(records, humanId)` with a short bound (it settled in about 4 s live; for example, 10 s) instead of `this.background(...)`, then answer from the outcome:
- not merged (`head_moved`/left_to_you): `{state:"refused", sentence: outcome.sentence}`, which is `headMovedSentence(40)`; the record, card and Tasks label stay as the step leaves them.
- merged: a merged sentence.
- still running at the bound: today's `Merging #N.`

Alternative, on the W15-05 pattern: a `headMovedNow(task, listedSha)` port beside `folderWaitNow` that calls `keepsOwnChange` and returns `headMovedSentence` when the change is not kept. The route then refuses before approving and asks the step to settle the record as head_moved, so the card and label still appear.

verified.root_cause:
The app writes this section into the brief itself; the model did not choose it. personNoteOn (packages/runtime/src/session/task-context.ts:127-145) looks for the newest change-log row that has a human_id, is not undone and has a command whose params name the task. It then returns that row's words_used (:141) as "the person's note", and taskContextBlock prints it under "## The person's note on this task" (:266-268). For changes made in the app, words_used is the Changes-page label the daemon fills in when no note was typed. Two examples: PUT /tasks/:id uses `body.note ?? \`Edit ${task.title}\`` (packages/runtime/src/daemon/server.ts:1197), and POST /tasks/:id/action uses `body.note ?? ACTION_WORDS[body.action]` (:1233). ACTION_WORDS (packages/runtime/src/daemon/task-words.ts:59) holds Redo, Try again, Resume, Stop, Go ahead without and the other button labels. verified.root_cause:
The model (claude-haiku-5-5, low effort, thinking off) made the false claim. The app sent it a context that made that claim likely, and nothing checks the reply afterwards. Three causes:

(1) The history keeps only the model's prose. historyMessages builds each earlier turn from t.human.text and t.reply.text alone (transcript.ts:197-204, used at agent.ts:855-861). The reply's actions (the change sentence 'Set web pages research may read ... Undo') and its tool_use and tool_result are dropped, even though TranscriptReply stores them as actions. The logged seq-3 request shows this: the earlier assistant message is just 'Done. For the Reading rules project, research may now only read developer.mozilla.org...'. That is a change claimed in plain text with no tool trace, which is exactly the pattern the model copied one turn later. Seq 4 had 'Yes to what? Nothing is waiting for your yes.' in its history, and there the model did call settings_set.

(2) The prompt the app sends invites a text-only answer to a widening request. conversation-agent.md:82-83 says 'You cannot widen budgets, permissions or autonomy by yourself; those commands ask the human through the runtime. Say so plainly when asked.' The settings_set definition (commands/settings.ts:686) adds 'one that widens it waits for the person's yes'. The rules forbid saying a setting changed without settings_set (conversation-agent.md:63-64, agent.ts:369 CHAT_RETRIEVAL_RULES). Nothing forbids saying a confirmation was requested, or that a change now waits for a yes, when no tool answered 'Needs confirmation'.

(3) No code guard. When the turn ran no command (results empty, pendingCard null, agent.ts:962 and 982-991), result.finalText reaches the person unchanged. That is how 'I've asked for confirmation ... Once you approve' was shown with no card, which breaks core-experience.md section 5 rules 4 and 9 (true now; no promises the code does not keep).

The rest of the observed behaviour is as designed: 'Yes to what?' because no card exists, and the read-back on the second try.

The evidence holds up. settings_set was among the 30 tools offered at seq 3: the finding's 'tools: []' means calls made, not tools offered. stopReason was end_turn, and the facts said open_requests: 0.

verified.root_cause:
The figure comes from fixed code, not from the model. The session review ran at tier 0 with critic_model 'none'. When the critic sends a task back, it goes back to ready, and the runner's replan() takes it again in the same session. replan() appends the new attempt to the session row's plan as a second item for the same task and adds that attempt's estimate to the plan total: items: [...current.items, ...cut.items], estimateUsdMicro: current.estimateUsdMicro + cut.estimateUsdMicro, then setPlan(...). The session review reads that grown total as "the plan's estimate": planEstimateOf returns plan.estimateUsdMicro. It then prints it as "against an estimate of".

Live evidence from the state.sqlite session row (01a1ddb7-ef9f…) agrees exactly. The plan holds two items for the same task: 142000 (the Start check's 113600 CHF micro, shown as "about CHF 0.11") and 126565 (the retry's "about CHF 0.10"). The plan total is 268565 USD micro, which is CHF 0.21. The review's metrics give estimateUsdMicro 268565 and the evidence says "plan: 2 item(s), estimate CHF 0.21".

A second effect of the same append: the review's only finding was its own low-severity "Plan lists the same task twice: Write the Swiss pairing tool with tests" (session-review.ts:244-245). That finding cost the grade 5 points (95 instead of 100), for the runner's own retry.

The finding's suspected cause is half right. session-review.ts does not add up the attempts' start estimates itself. The runner's re-plan adds each retry's estimate into the stored plan total, and the review trusts that total.

verified.root_cause:
sameTitleTags (packages/commands/src/commands/task.ts:127-161) builds only one kind of qualifier for a group of tasks that share a title. It uses pull requests when every task has its own (line 132), otherwise states when all of them differ (line 139), and falls back to age ("older"/"newer", then ordinals) only when the states are equal (lines 145-160). findTask (lines 210-214) tests the person's word only against that kind's `says` regex.

With two ready tasks the refusal offers "(the older one)", and that wording does pick the older task. Pausing it gives the two tasks different states (needs_human and ready), so sameTitleTags switches to state tags: `^paused$` and `^ready$`. "older" now matches neither, hit.length is 0, `matches` is empty (no title contains the whole phrase "write the guide (the older one)"), and lines 220-221 send the new state-based refusal.

The model is not involved. c1c.json shows "calls": [] (the parser handled the line itself), and the reply is sameTitleRefusal's text word for word.

Reproduced at the command boundary, at the base and at head (scripts /tmp/frbench/l3run6/repro.mts and repro-head.mts):
- pause "Write the guide (the older one)" → done, and the older task is the one paused.
- reopen "Write the guide (the older one)" → refused "…the paused one and the ready one…".
- resume "Write the guide (the older one)" → the same refusal.
- resume "(the paused one)" → done.

The same thing happens in the other tiers:
- "the done one" stops picking once both tasks have their own pull request.
- "older" stops picking when a third task with the same title arrives, because the tags become first/second/third.

Keep what the refusal says, and change what picks a task. In findTask, when group.length > 1, test the word against every kind of tag that tells the tasks apart:
- a task's PR number (when the task has a PR and no other task in the group has the same number);
- its state word (when no other task in the group is in that state);
- its age word, always ("older|oldest|first|1st" and "newer|newest|latest|last|second|2nd" for two tasks, ordinals for three or more).

Return the task when exactly one task in the group matches any of them. One way to do it: a sameTitlePickers(group) helper that returns, per task, a list of `says` regexes; sameTitleTags keeps choosing the single most telling tag for the sentence.

A word from an earlier refusal then keeps working after a pause, a PR or a state change. Each kind's words are disjoint ("#17", state words, age words), so one word never picks two different tasks.

verified.root_cause:
For JavaScript, the only test runner Forerunner's checks know is a package.json `test` script. A folder that has JS test files and no package.json gets the 'told' line and nothing runs. Python, Rust and Go already have marker checks that run with no config at all: Python's stdlib unittest runs even when there is no pyproject. That breaks the owner's C-3 / ADR 0104 / ADR 0110 decision that a code task's tests always run, whatever the language. The code path:
- `projectChecks` returns no checks when there is no package.json (project-checks.ts:75-78).
- `markerChecks` (project-checks.ts:311-399) has Python, Rust and Go entries but none for JavaScript.
- `untestedFiles` (project-checks.ts:409-430) returns exactly 'the project has test files (wc.test.js) that no check ran: there is no package.json to run them' (:419).
- critic.ts:438-443 adds that line to `evidence.notChecked`, which is what the drawer's 'See what was checked' shows.
- The try plan cannot pick up the README's `node --test` either: `parseCommand` only accepts `node <script>.js` (try-plan.ts:117-118, :392), so `node --test` is dropped without a word, from the criterion as well as from the README. Also, the README only counts when the task changed it (try-plan.ts:181 searches changedFiles), and the tester task did not change it.

The app's own prompts made this choice likely, so it is not the model alone. The README with '## Tests ```node --test```' was already in the 'Workspace before "Write wc.js word counter"' commit (36cd1bd), so the intake plan wrote it, not a specialist. That plan also wrote the criterion '`node --test` passes', because the intake prompt says 'say ... which check must pass' (intake.ts:1962) without saying which checks Forerunner can run. The tester's brief (verification.ts:78) does truthfully say JS checks are 'its package.json scripts'. But its own criterion said 'runnable with `node --test`', and its sibling task said 'only Node.js built-in modules'. Writing no package.json was therefore the natural result, and the run's README and docs/testing.md both name `node --test` as the project's test command.

The critic's own text confirms the gap: 'The runtime did not run node --test; the pass claim rests on the worker's report'. ADR 0110 rule 5 designed the told line for the case of 'a package.json that names no test script'. W15-50 later made that line accurate for a folder with no package.json, but nobody decided whether such a folder's node:test files should run. An existing unit test, packages/runtime/test/try-plan.test.ts:639-660 ('W15-50'), asserts the current line; I ran it and it passes at 7d6b34a. The by-hand evidence (6 of 6 pass) also holds: wc.test.js only uses node:test plus child_process, and Node 22 finds it with no arguments.
